title: Reverse a String
description:
Given a string `s`, return it written backwards.

Example: for `s = "hello"` return `"olleh"`.

Spaces and other characters are reversed too, just like letters.
hints: Concept: a string is a sequence of characters, a lot like an array. `s.length()` gives its size and `s.charAt(i)` gives the character at position `i`.
Approach: walk through the string from the last character to the first, adding each character to a new string as you go. A `StringBuilder` is the efficient way to build a string piece by piece.

Pseudocode:
  builder = empty
  for i from length - 1 down to 0:
      append s.charAt(i) to builder
  return builder as a string

workedExample.title: Remove All Spaces
workedExample.description: Return `s` with every space character removed. `"a b c"` becomes `"abc"`.
workedExample.explanation:
Strings in Java can't be changed once created, so the usual pattern is to build a new one with a `StringBuilder`, appending the characters you want.

This loop goes front to back. For reversing, you'd go back to front instead.

walkthrough.note: Start at the last position (4). Append 'o'.
i = 0: append 'h'. The loop ends, so return "olleh".

mistakes.hint: The text came out in the same order. Start from the last character, `s.length() - 1`, and count down.
Your loop starts one past the end. The last character is at `s.length() - 1`.
